subject: Clarify: training usage guarantees, data residency, and deletion playbook
messages:
From: Katherine Lopez <katie.lopez@insurepay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@insurepay.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify training/no-train + retention windows (procurement request)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. Procurement needs explicit confirmation on two points before we can finalize the SOW:

1) Do you use customer-provided request/response data to train or fine-tune any of Redwood's models (hosted or dedicated) by default? If you say no, please describe any narrow exceptions (opt-ins, aggregated telemetry, safety datasets) and the process to opt out.

2) We need a retention breakdown for customer data types: request payloads, response text, KV/prefix caches, logs/traces, backups/snapshots, and long-term audit logs. For each item please state default retention and any cross-region replication windows.

I've attached the procurement security checklist — they want short, prescriptive answers and an exportable artifact we can keep with the contract. Can you also indicate what evidence we can supply to show deletion occurred (export or attestation)?

Best,
Katherine
Senior Procurement Manager
InsurePay
(attachment: security-checklist.pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Katherine Lopez <katie.lopez@insurepay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training/no-train + retention windows (procurement request)

Katherine,

Short answers up front:
- Training: By default, Redwood does NOT use customer request/response data to train or fine-tune our models. No customer content is incorporated into model training unless a customer explicitly opts in via a documented program.
- Retention: We keep short operational traces and request bodies for limited windows (details below) and maintain separate audit logs for compliance. Backups and DR snapshots are handled with strict retention and deletion procedures.

Details and edge cases:
1) Training usage and telemetry
- Default policy: Customer data from hosted API calls (request/response text, files, embeddings) is not used to update model weights, retrain, or fine-tune models.
- Opt-in programs: If a customer enrolls in a model-improvement program, participation is explicit, documented, and reversible. Enrollment requires legal and product approval; we keep a record of consent.
- Aggregated telemetry: We may collect anonymized, aggregated metrics (latency percentiles, token counts, error classes) to improve service reliability. This telemetry contains no customer text content.

2) Retention matrix (default, per-hosted account):
- Request/response payloads (full bodies): 90 days default; can be shortened via contract for dedicated/private deployments.
- KV/prefix caches (runtime only): Ephemeral — typical TTL < 1 hour; not stored persistently to disk outside of transient caches.
- Request metadata & traces (headers, timestamps, routing, error traces): 30 days default for troubleshooting.
- Backups / snapshots (storage-level snapshots used for recovery): 90 days; periodic snapshots replicated to a secondary region for DR (replica retention 7 days).
- Long-term audit logs (auth events, admin actions): 365 days default to support compliance and incident investigations.
- Billing records (token counts, invoice history): 13 months to support financial reconciliation.

3) Deletion / export / evidence
- Deletion workflow: Customer files a support request (or uses Console > Data > Erase). We create a ticket, schedule object-level deletes in the account bucket, and purge snapshots that reference the objects. Deletion is both logical (remove pointers) and physical (delete objects from object storage), with a playbook for verifying deletion from live and DR copies.
- Evidence: We can provide an export manifest (list of deleted object keys and deletion timestamps) and an optional signed attestation on request. For enterprise customers we offer a downloadable deletion report within 72 hours of completion.
- Exceptions: For legal hold or active investigations we can pause deletion after notifying the customer.

We can turn this into a short, stamped attestation and an exportable deletion report for procurement. Vivek / Neha: flag anything I've missed on snapshots or exports.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — helpful. A couple of follow-ups from Legal & Procurement:

- Can you confirm whether snapshots/backups used for DR are encrypted with a customer-managed key (KMS/HSM) or a Redwood-managed key?
- For the 90-day snapshot retention, are there any hidden copies (e.g., object lifecycle transitions or archival tiers) that would keep data beyond 90 days?
- Procurement needs the timeline for an exportable deletion report and wants to know whether the deletion process includes the secondary DR replica. Finally, Legal would like a short attestation we can attach to the contract (one paragraph + deletion evidence availability).

If you can send a short playbook or checklist we can attach that will go a long way.

-Katherine

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify: training/no-train + retention windows (procurement request) — playbook and attestations

Katherine — thanks, quick playbook and the attestation language below. I'm attaching a concise deletion/export instructions file for your ops team.

DR encryption & keys:
- All customer storage at rest is encrypted. By default, snapshots and object storage use Redwood-managed KMS keys. Customer-managed keys (CMK) are available for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers; for hosted customers we offer CMK as an add-on and can document key rotation windows in the contract.
- We do not retain additional hidden archival copies beyond the stated snapshot lifecycle; lifecycle policies move objects to archival tiers only if explicitly configured by the customer account. Default managed accounts do not auto-archive beyond the 90-day snapshot retention.

Snapshot & DR deletes:
- Primary: snapshot references are removed and underlying objects scheduled for deletion within the 72-hour sweep job.
- DR replica: we schedule replica purge as part of the same ticket; replication deletions are queued and completed within the same 7-day window used for DR retention. We include DR replica keys in the deletion manifest.

Exportable deletion report (playbook summary):
1) Customer opens a support/erase request (Console or Support ticket).
2) Ops creates a deletion ticket and identifies object keys, snapshots, and any cross-region replicas.
3) We snapshot the deletion plan and submit to internal compliance for approval (same day).
4) Physical object deletes and snapshot purges are executed (0–72 hours) and queued for DR replica purge (completed within 7 days).
5) We return a signed deletion manifest (list of object keys, bucket paths, deletion timestamps, and confirming auditor id). Standard SLA: manifest delivered within 48 hours of completion; attestation available within 72 hours on request.

Retention nuance notes (important for procurement language):
- Operational traces and short-term debugging artifacts are retained for 30 days to allow incident triage. These are not fed into models.
- We retain long-term audit logs (365 days) for security/compliance; audit logs contain metadata about actions, not the full request/response bodies.
- Billing records are retained for 13 months and are required for invoicing and dispute resolution.
- For Dedicated/Private customers we can negotiate shortened retention windows and exclusive regional residency.

One-paragraph attestation (suggested contract language):
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided request or response data to train, fine-tune, or improve model weights except where the customer has explicitly opted into a documented program. Customer data is stored in the region selected at account creation and is subject to the retention and deletion controls described in the Redwood Data Residency and Retention Policy. Upon request Redwood will execute the documented deletion playbook and provide a signed deletion manifest confirming deletion from primary and DR replicas."

Next steps: I can produce a formal signed attestation PDF and the deletion manifest flow for Legal. If helpful, we can set a 30-min call with Vivek (platform security) and Neha (ops) to walk procurement through the playbook.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
